newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Demirbank targets 30 percent growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turk Demirbank targets 30 percent growth in 1997.

text.p: Turk Demirbank T.A.S. targets to increase its total assets 30 percent in 1997, from $856 million in 1996, a senior company official said.

"We exceeded our 30 percent 1996 growth target by reaching approximately 50 percent growth rate and our growth target for 1997 is again 30 percent," Selahattin Serbest, general manager of the bank, told Reuters.
The bank will open more than 10 branches this year to raise the number of its branches to 50 by year-end, after setting up 10 new branches and raising the total figure to 36 in 1996.
"This will help us to meet our growth target. More branches mean more customers and faster growth," Serbest said.
The bank plans new branches in Turkey's leading industrial and export centres like Izmit, Denizli, Kahramanmaras, Adana, Mersin and Ankara.

Demirbank's growth was mainly based on the expansion in lending and other "real banking activities" like interests on credits and commissions charged on services, Serbest said, adding that treasury operations also contributed to income.

"For example our total loans rose by 86 percent in real terms to represent 32 percent of our total assets. On the other hand, our securities portfolio makes up only 19 percent of the total assets," he added.
Turkish banking system made good profits from treasury operations in 1996, benefiting from real interest rates of up to 40 percent.
Demirbank owns 75 percent of Demir-Halkbank based in the Netherlands and 25 percent of Romlease Leasing in Romania.

It will control 50 percent of Demirkyrgyz Bank to be opened in Kyrgyzstan in the first quarter of 1997. Fifteen percent of the venture will be owned by International Finance Corporation, 15 percent by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, 10 percent by FOM of the Netherlands and 10 percent by a local investor.

Demirbank reported 10.03 trillion lira of net profits in 1996, up 120 percent up from 4.56 trillion lira in 1995. Its total assets leapt to 146.19 trillion lira last year, from 51.11 trillion lira in 1995.
